chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not forget the two duties', or he said: 'It is upon you to adhere to the two duties at the end of every prayer.' I said, 'And what are the two duties?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Asking Allah for Paradise and seeking Refuge with Allah from the Fire.'

key_terms.الْمُوجِبَتَيْنِ: The two duties/obligations (referring to the two supplications)
key_terms.دُبُرِ: After/behind (referring to the time immediately following the prayer)

ai.seo_question: What are the two specific supplications recommended after every prayer in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) emphasizes the 'two duties' (al-mujibatan) of seeking Paradise and refuge from Hellfire as a consistent post-prayer practice, highlighting the transition from ritual worship to personal supplication. This instruction underscores the Shia scholarly view that the immediate aftermath of Salah is a critical moment for securing one's eternal fate, linking the physical act of prayer with the spiritual aspiration for Jannah and the avoidance of Jahannam.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Zurara who said,

‘Abu Ja’farasws said: ‘Do not forget the two duties’, or said: ‘It is upon you with the two duties at the end of every Salāt’. I said, ‘And what are the two duties?’ Heasws said: ‘Your asking Allahazwj for the Paradise, and seeking Refuge with Allahazwj from the Fire’.
en.sarwar: 19. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz from Zurarah, who has said the following:

“Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Do not forget’ - or that he said ‘you must not forget appealing before Allah after every obligatory Salah (prayer) about the two essential matters.’ I then asked, ‘What are the two essential matters?’ The Imam replied, ‘Appealing before Allah for paradise and seeking refuge with Allah against the fire.”’
